chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Salim, from Ibn Maskin, from Ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: I heard him say:
Allah was, and there was nothing else, and He has always been Knowing of what He created. His knowledge of them before their creation is like His knowledge of them after He created them.
ai.seo_question: What does Shia theology say about Allah's knowledge before and after creation?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Baqir (AS) elucidates the attribute of Divine Knowledge (Ilm) by affirming that Allah existed before creation, with His knowledge of potentialities being identical to His knowledge of actualities. It underscores the constancy and perfection of His knowledge, a key concept in Shia theology distinguishing between His essential attributes and His actions. This perspective highlights the unchanging nature of God's awareness, which remains constant regardless of the temporal unfolding of creation.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 12. My father (RA) said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-`Attar said, on the authority of Muhammad ibn alHusayn ibn Abu al-Khattab, on the authority of Ibn Abu `Umayr, on the authority of Hisham ibn Salim, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Muslim that I heard Abu Ja`far al-Baqir (AS) say:

“Allah was there when there was nothing other than Him. He has always been All-Knowing of what He has created. Therefore, His Knowledge of things before their being is exactly the same as His Knowledge of things after their creation.”
